title: Relative section cone, supports, and change of topology
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j:W=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on either small site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ or $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. An abelian sheaf means a contravariant functor to abelian groups satisfying the sheaf equalizer condition for covering families. For an abelian sheaf $F$ and a nonnegative injective resolution $F	o I^ ullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], put $A^q=I^q(T)$, $B^q=I^q(W)$, $r=\operatorname{res}:A^ ullet	o B^ ullet$, and $K^ ullet=\ker r$. Extend section complexes by zero in negative degrees. Form the relative section complex $C^q=A^q\oplus B^{q-1}$ with $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$, the signed model of $\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$ [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $A^ ullet$ and $B^ ullet$ compute derived sections on $T$ and $W$, and the inclusion $K^ ullet	o C^ ullet$, $k\mapsto(k,0)$, is a quasi-isomorphism. It canonically identifies relative cohomology $H^q(C^ ullet)$ with $R^q\Gamma_Z(T,F)$, where $\Gamma_Z(T,F)=\ker(F(T)	o F(W))$, the support convention of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Under this identification the projection $C^ ullet	o A^ ullet$ is forgetting support and the localization boundary is represented by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. These comparisons are independent of resolutions and commute with coefficient morphisms, restriction along etale neighbourhoods, and inclusions $W'\subseteq W$ (enlargement of support). Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For any abelian etale sheaf $F$, the canonical derived-section pullbacks on $T$ and $W$ induce an isomorphism $H^q(T,W;F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T_{\mathrm{proet}},W_{\mathrm{proet}};
u_T^{-1}F)$ for every $q\geq0$, commuting with forgetting support, localization boundary, coefficient morphisms, etale restriction and enlargement of support. Here the pro-etale relative group uses the identical signed section-cone construction. For a pro-etale coefficient morphism $
u_T^{-1}F	o F'$, composition gives the same compatibilities with the supported class in $R^q\Gamma_Z(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F')$.

proof.text: On either chosen site, restriction of each injective term along the given open monomorphism is epimorphic by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-mono-restriction]. The supported-section complex is the kernel of this restriction: verify the universal property degreewise, including the zero terms in negative degrees. Thus the restriction fits into a short exact sequence of complexes. The injective-resolution convention [def-sp-injective-resolutions] computes the relevant derived section functors.

Apply [lem-weil-degreewise-epi-kernel-cocone-qis] to obtain the kernel-to-shifted-cone quasi-isomorphism with components (k,0). These coordinates determine the map uniquely. Identify the kernel with the supported-section complex from Step 1. The coordinate equations show that its composite with cone projection is the kernel inclusion. The complete cycle calculation in [lem-pur-kernel-shifted-cone-boundary] identifies the shifted cone inclusion with the connecting morphism of the kernel short exact sequence, including the shift-homology identification. This proves the signed localization-boundary formula.

Define the support realization as the inverse of homology of the kernel-to-cone quasi-isomorphism, followed by the inverse kernel identification and the inverse injective-resolution computation isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. This gives the required normalization. Naturality of the derived-functor computation gives forgetting support, coefficient maps and object/support restriction maps. For every commuting restriction square, compare the induced kernel map and cone map by their two components; the (k,0) equations make the square commute. Applying homology yields all the single-site System equations.

Write L and G for the comparison adjoints [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Exactness of L makes L(I) a resolution, so the standard injective-resolution lifting construction produces an augmented lift β:L(I)→K. This lift is a quasi-isomorphism. Each term L(I^n) is G-acyclic by [lem-cbc-abelian-comparison-injective-acyclicity], and each injective K^n is G-acyclic. The acyclic-resolution comparison criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], in the already-proved source API Functor.quasiIso_map_of_rightAcyclic_nat, therefore makes Gβ a quasi-isomorphism. The unit is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-unit], so its composite ψβ:I→G(K) is a quasi-isomorphism. Since G is right adjoint to the exact functor L, G preserves injectives. A quasi-isomorphism between these nonnegative complexes of injectives is a homotopy equivalence by CochainComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_injective. Every additive functor, including evaluation at any etale object and supported sections, preserves this homotopy equivalence. Extension by zero preserves the resulting quasi-isomorphism. Consequently the section and supported-section comparison maps are isomorphisms on homology. The kernel/cone comparison square from Step 3 then gives the cone isomorphism directly.

For an arbitrary pro-etale coefficient map γ, the two transposed augmented lifts I→G(K) agree on the augmentation. They are homotopic because the source augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and the target terms are injective. Apply supported sections, extend the homotopy by zero, and use the homology square of Step 3; cancel its invertible kernel-to-cone map to obtain lift independence. The same argument compares β′ with β followed by a coefficient-resolution lift, proving postcomposition. For simultaneous etale and pro-etale coefficient maps, unit naturality makes the two resulting maps into G(K₁) agree on the augmentation; their homotopy gives the coefficient equation. Object restriction squares commute strictly by naturality of sheaf morphisms, and functoriality of mapArrowHom gives the cone square. The cone projection and shifted inclusion commute with every cone map by their component formulas. These prove every TopologyComparison field. Specialize the single-site realization to the open complement of the closed immersion to obtain the asserted e and its normalization.

proof_origin.place: The support-boundary and comparison clauses, formalized by B8 using kernel/cone coordinates and the transposed injective-resolution lift. Step 4 uses the existing acyclic-resolution API and the Grothendieck comparison unit; it avoids the Leray-edge and five-lemma detour. The independent boundary calculation is lem-pur-kernel-shifted-cone-boundary.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 needs the generic injective-sheaf restriction-surjectivity lemma for the monomorphism W→T; no node in the Kummer unit supplies this site-theoretic fact.
Step 4 needs the general comparison isomorphism for arbitrary abelian sheaves on T and W; the Kummer unit has no replacement for this comparison.
Step 4 needs the object-level definition and naturality of the site cohomology pullback at the object W; generic site cohomology, not supplied by the Kummer unit.
Step 4 needs exactness of the abelian inverse image to form the comparison chain map; generic site fact.
Step 4 needs the unit F->nu_* nu^{-1}F to be bijective on etale sections to run the comparison at the object W.
Step 4 needs nu_*-acyclicity of nu^{-1}I for injective etale I to obtain R^q nu_*(nu^{-1}F)=0.
Step 4 computes R^q nu_* by the acyclic resolution nu^{-1}I; generic derived-functor criterion.
Step 4 needs the degenerate-Leray edge isomorphism at the object W, which lem-cbc only states for the terminal object.

lean.statement: theorem relativeConeSupportComparison (T : Scheme.{u}) {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i] (F : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (I : InjectiveResolution F) : ∃ (E : RelativeCone.System T.smallEtaleTopology (fun {_ _} f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left)) (P : RelativeCone.System (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (fun {V _} f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left ∧ Etale V.hom)) (e : ∀ q : ℕ, relativeCohomology T (Scheme.Etale.mk i.openComplement.ι) I q ≅ supportCohomology i q F), Nonempty (RelativeCone.TopologyComparison T E P) ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, (e q).hom = ((E.realization (supportRestrictionArrow i) (by change IsOpenImmersion i.openComplement.ι; infer_instance) I).e q).hom
